Shorten the nightly ingestion interval so the current circular is added more often than the superseded one.

q: A screening service receives outcome labels 45 days after each decision. This week, the proportion of missing employment records and the proportion of scores near the decision boundary both increase. No verified outcomes are yet available for the affected requests. A manager asks whether this proves that the relationship between employment and eligibility has changed and therefore justifies immediate retraining. Which conclusion and next step are most defensible?
o: The signals justify investigation but do not establish concept drift; check upstream data quality and feature consistency now, then assess predictive performance when valid outcomes are available.
The simultaneous movements establish concept drift; retrain immediately using the current predictions as substitute labels for the missing outcomes.
The absence of an accuracy alert establishes that model quality is unchanged; postpone all investigation until the next labelled evaluation.
A wider distribution of scores proves improved discrimination; reduce monitoring sensitivity to avoid reacting to normal model adaptation.

q: A synchronous service must achieve p90 latency of at most 800 ms at its observed peak of 200 requests per second. A proposed model has p90 latency of 610 ms at 80 requests per second. At 200 requests per second, the vendor reports only mean latency of 470 ms. Hosting, cost and explanation requirements have already been validated. What should the deployment reviewer conclude?
o: The latency requirement is met because a mean of 470 ms guarantees that at least 90% of requests finish within 800 ms.
The latency requirement is violated because latency must increase in exact proportion to requests per second.
Compliance is not yet established; obtain the required latency percentile from a representative load test at 200 requests per second.
The latency requirement is met because the measured p90 at the lower load already leaves 190 ms of headroom.

q: A team replaces names in Restricted case files with random identifiers before sending them to an external summarisation service. The files still contain detailed employment histories and rare combinations of case circumstances. The entity's policy requires the approved environment for these files unless an authorised reclassification or exception is completed. Neither has occurred. Which assessment is correct?
o: Replacing names automatically reclassifies the files because the external provider cannot see the original identifier mapping.
The transformation guarantees anonymity because no single remaining field directly states the person's legal name.
Transfer is permitted if the vendor deletes the generated summary, even when it processes the source files outside the approved environment.
Removing direct identifiers does not establish anonymity or change the stated handling requirement; obtain the required approval or keep processing inside the approved environment.

q: A model predicts whether an application will be withdrawn within 30 days. To make retraining more current, an engineer adds applications submitted during the last five days and labels every case without a recorded withdrawal as negative. Most of these applications are still open. After deployment, predicted withdrawal rates fall sharply, although the operational process has not changed. What is the primary defect?
o: Recent applications should always be excluded from machine-learning datasets because they necessarily differ from older applications.
Outcomes that have not had time to mature are being treated as confirmed negatives; respect the outcome window or use a method that explicitly handles incomplete follow-up.
The model has become underconfident because its training set is larger; increase model capacity before changing label construction.
The production threshold is too high; lower it until the predicted withdrawal rate matches the historical rate.

q: A controlled experiment improves successful task completion by 2.4 percentage points, with a 95% confidence interval of +1.0 to +3.8 points. However, incorrect eligibility advice increases by 0.8 percentage points, with a 95% confidence interval of +0.4 to +1.2 points. The pre-agreed release rule prohibits an increase greater than 0.2 percentage points in incorrect advice. Other operational requirements pass, and the planned analysis is complete. What is the correct decision?
o: Promote the variant because the lower confidence bound for task completion is positive and therefore the model is better overall.
Promote the variant after describing incorrect advice as a known limitation because the absolute increase is below one percentage point.
Withhold promotion because the incorrect-advice increase exceeds the agreed guardrail; the task-completion improvement does not override that condition.
Ignore the guardrail result until its confidence interval excludes zero by a larger margin than the task- completion interval.

q: A model's weights are quantised, reducing measured weight memory from 18 GiB to 6 GiB. The service has 24 GiB of usable GPU memory and requires 4 GiB of other fixed allocations. At the intended sequence length, each active session still needs 0.5 GiB of KV cache. Forty sessions must be active simultaneously. Assume no cache sharing and no other allocations for this calculation. Which statement is correct?
o: The configuration still requires 30 GiB; reducing weight precision alone does not make the unchanged session-cache requirement fit.
The configuration requires 10 GiB because KV caches are already included in the measured quantised weight memory.
The configuration requires 20 GiB because weights and runtime allocations are replaced by the active sessions' caches.
The configuration fits because reducing weight memory by two-thirds necessarily reduces total serving memory by the same fraction.

q: A candidate classifier satisfies the required accuracy, latency, cost and hosting conditions. It produces fluent rejection rationales, but an explanation audit finds that these rationales repeatedly name a feature whose value did not influence the corresponding decision. The release requirements include validated per-decision explanations, and the candidate has not passed that validation. How should the review team proceed?
o: Accept the rationales because their readability is sufficient evidence that applicants can understand how the model reached each decision.
Treat explanation validation as an unmet requirement and resolve it before approval; persuasive wording does not establish that a rationale reflects the actual decision.
Approve deployment because high predictive accuracy makes the fidelity of individual rejection explanations operationally irrelevant.
Add a second language model to rewrite the rationales and treat improved fluency as completion of the explanation audit.

q: After a prompt-injection incident involving hidden document text, a team changes its PDF parser to remove invisible content. A subsequent authorised test places the same instruction in a normal visible paragraph. The assistant again treats the paragraph as authority to request an internal record. The retrieval tool uses the assistant's broad service account rather than enforcing the requesting user's permissions. What should be fixed next?
o: Reject every document containing imperative verbs and keep the retrieval tool's existing service- account permissions.
Convert uploaded documents to images and allow unrestricted retrieval whenever the instruction arrives through OCR.
Add a warning that uploaded documents may contain instructions and let the model decide which permissions those instructions require.
Enforce the user's access permissions at the retrieval boundary and treat document instructions as untrusted, regardless of whether their text is visible.

q: A deployment packages fine-tuned model weights with a tokenizer copied from a different release. Both tokenizers have the same vocabulary size, so startup succeeds. However, a comparison shows that several token IDs, including role-related special tokens, map to different strings. Responses contain malformed conversational boundaries and unrelated fragments even when generation is deterministic. Which action should come first?
o: Restore the tokenizer and special-token configuration paired with the trained weights, and verify the complete model-tokenizer-template bundle.
Increase the sampling temperature so the model can compensate for the changed token mappings through a wider choice of outputs.
Continue using the replacement tokenizer because equal vocabulary sizes establish compatibility with the model's learned embeddings.
Remove conversational instructions from the input and retain the incompatible token mappings to simplify the serving interface.

q: Two candidate models satisfy every documented release requirement. Model A is cheaper and faster; Model B has higher F1. The requirements specify only minimum F1 and maximum cost and latency, with no ranking rule among feasible candidates. The sponsor prioritises service quality, while the operations lead prioritises cost. The team is asked to identify the uniquely correct production choice from the existing requirements. What is the most appropriate response?
o: Select Model B because higher F1 always takes precedence once all candidates satisfy the documented operational constraints.
Select Model A because the least expensive feasible model is always the professionally correct choice for public services.
Explain that the current requirements do not determine a unique choice, present the trade- off and obtain an agreed selection objective from the accountable stakeholders.
Average the models' normalised scores using weights chosen by the engineer and describe the resulting ranking as already approved.

q: A replacement model performs correctly in offline replay but produces overly optimistic scores for applications with missing income histories in production. The training transform imputes these values with a fitted median; the serving adapter substitutes zero. Replaying the production feature vectors through the offline model reproduces the optimistic scores. The previous deployment remains available, and the affected cases can be identified. Which response best isolates the defect while limiting further impact?
o: Retrain immediately on the optimistic production scores so the next model learns the behaviour of the serving adapter.
Lower every application's score by a fixed amount, then use aggregate accuracy to decide whether the incident is resolved.
Retain the replacement for all traffic and change its architecture because the replay establishes insufficient model capacity.
Restore the validated path for affected traffic, align the serving transform with the fitted training transform, and verify parity using the same replay cases.

q: An engineering team fixes an assistant that occasionally returns an internal routing schema to citizens. The defect came from one endpoint overwriting response-format settings used by another. Separate sequential tests had always passed. A proposed regression test merely checks that the assistant's final displayed text is not enclosed in braces; the frontend can strip those braces even when the backend returns the wrong structure. Which test would most directly prevent recurrence of the underlying defect?
o: Interleave requests to both endpoints and assert their independently expected request configurations and response contracts, including isolation under concurrency.
Increase the number of sequential conversational examples while keeping the routing endpoint inactive during the entire test run.
Verify that the frontend removes punctuation from every response so a structured object cannot be visually recognised by the user.
Check only that both endpoints call the same model identifier because a pinned model guarantees consistent endpoint-specific output formats.

q: A policy assistant must answer both current questions and historical audit questions. Circular V1 applied from January through June; V2 took effect in July. Both are authoritative and must remain available for audit. When asked which rule applied to a case decided in March, the assistant returns V2 because the retrieval system always selects the most recently published version. Which retrieval policy is appropriate?
o: Delete V1 permanently because retaining superseded documents necessarily makes retrieval unreliable.
Resolve the question's relevant date and retrieve the version effective at that time, while using current-document eligibility for current-policy questions.
Retrieve whichever version has the highest semantic similarity and let the generator infer its applicability without date metadata.
Always prefer V2 and add a general warning that the assistant's answers may not describe the rules that applied historically.

q: A model scores applications at 09:00 each morning. An employment event occurred on Monday but did not arrive in the entity's data platform until Thursday. A training reconstruction for Tuesday includes that event because its event timestamp is before Tuesday's prediction time. The production service could not have accessed the record on Tuesday. Many historical records are backfilled in this way. Which change repairs the leakage?
o: Randomise the training rows before splitting so delayed records are distributed equally between training and validation.
Keep the event because its real-world occurrence preceded the prediction, and add stronger regularisation to reduce its influence.
Split the same reconstructed table chronologically and retain every feature whose event timestamp precedes its prediction timestamp.
Reconstruct features using what was actually available by each prediction cutoff, accounting for arrival or availability time as well as event time.

q:
An entity has approved a cost-minimisation objective: select the least expensive candidate with F1 of at least 0.85 and p95 latency no greater than 900 ms at the required peak load. Every candidate has approved hosting and validated explanations. The measurements below use the same held-out set and workload.
Model | F1 | p95 at peak | Monthly cost
A | 0.86 | 880 ms | SAR 18,000
B | 0.89 | 820 ms | SAR 26,000
C | 0.84 | 500 ms | SAR 14,000
Which selection follows the approved objective?
o: Model B, because higher F1 takes precedence over cost even when the required quality floor is already met.
Model C, because the lowest cost compensates for its small shortfall against the minimum F1 requirement.
Model A, because it meets the quality and latency requirements at a lower cost than the other feasible candidate.
No model, because a candidate must simultaneously achieve the highest F1, lowest latency and lowest cost to be acceptable.

q: A replacement assistant reduces overall factual errors from 5% to 3%. However, in a separately evaluated category involving urgent application deadlines, incorrect deadline advice rises from 0.4% to 2.0%. The approved release rule limits that category's error rate to 1%. The evaluation is sufficiently large to meet the protocol's decision requirements. A product owner argues that the lower overall error rate makes the replacement safer. What is the correct assessment?
o: The replacement should be approved because a lower aggregate error rate establishes improvement for every operationally important category.
The aggregate improvement does not satisfy the category-specific requirement; block that scope or remediate and revalidate the failure before approving it.
The deadline category should be merged into the overall evaluation because separate reporting gives a small category disproportionate influence.
A disclaimer about possible deadline errors is sufficient to replace the category-specific acceptance condition without further approval.

q:
An unchanged classifier's aggregate accuracy falls from 92% to 83%. An audit using mature labels and consistent category definitions produces the following results.
Previous workload | Current workload
Case category | Previous accuracy | Current accuracy
share | share
Routine | 80% | 20% | 95% | 95%
Complex | 20% | 80% | 80% | 80%
Which interpretation is best supported?
o: The model's accuracy has deteriorated within both categories, establishing that its feature-to- outcome relationships have changed.
The aggregate decline is a monitoring error because unchanged category-level accuracy requires unchanged overall accuracy.
The model must have suffered a serving-code regression because a workload shift cannot change an aggregate evaluation metric.
The aggregate decline is explained by the larger share of complex cases; assess service suitability for the new mix without claiming a demonstrated within-category performance drop.

q: A team measures p95 latency separately for three sequential stages: retrieval at 150 ms, inference at 500 ms and validation at 70 ms. The end-to-end service requirement is p95 no greater than 800 ms at peak load. An engineer adds the three reported percentiles to obtain 720 ms and declares the service compliant. No end-to-end latency distribution has been measured. Which response is technically justified?
o: Accept the claim because percentiles of sequential stages always add in the same way as the durations of one particular request.
Reject the service because the true end-to-end p95 must always exceed the sum of the individual stage p95 values.
Compliance is not established by adding marginal percentiles; measure end-to-end latency over representative peak-load requests.
Use the largest individual stage p95 as the end-to-end p95 because only the slowest stage determines a sequential request's duration.

q: A fine-tuned model generates repeated question fragments in production. The base model answers correctly in a vendor playground, but the playground also uses a different conversation template and decoding configuration. The team suspects that the production template does not match fine-tuning. Management requests an experiment that distinguishes this explanation from a problem in the fine- tuned weights. Which comparison is most informative first?
o: Run identical requests through the same fine-tuned weights and decoding settings, varying only between the production template and the verified training-compatible template.
Compare the base model at high temperature with the fine-tuned model at low temperature, using each environment's default template.
Retrain the model with a larger dataset and compare the result with yesterday's production traffic without preserving the earlier prompts.
Ask reviewers which environment's responses sound more natural while changing templates, model versions and decoding settings together.

q: Following a provider migration, an assistant's billed input tokens increase even though the document collection and user traffic are unchanged. Direct tokenisation of the same final text produces nearly identical counts with both tokenizers, and token prices are unchanged. A trace comparison shows that the new request adapter inserts twelve retrieved passages where the old adapter inserted four. Long requests now exceed the configured context budget. What is the most likely explanation and first correction?
o: The new tokenizer must be less efficient for Arabic; replace it before investigating the assembled request payload.
The assembled prompts contain substantially more retrieved content; align retrieval and prompt-assembly budgets and validate the complete request size.
The model has more parameters, so the provider counts the same input token several times during each forward pass.
The context limit has become character-based; reduce the number of Unicode characters without inspecting the extra passages.

q:
A review team can process at most 180 alerts on any day, and deferring cases to the next day is not permitted. The approved objective is the highest recall among thresholds that fit both ordinary and peak-day workloads. The following planning estimates have been validated for the expected operating range.
Threshold | Average daily alerts | Peak-day alerts | Recall
0.35 | 240 | 360 | 78%
0.50 | 140 | 230 | 65%
0.65 | 100 | 170 | 52%
0.80 | 70 | 110 | 37%
Which threshold satisfies the decision rule?
o: 0.35, because the highest recall should determine the threshold before capacity constraints are considered.
0.50, because its average volume is below capacity and average compliance is sufficient for the stated daily requirement.
0.80, because leaving the largest unused capacity must take precedence over recall among feasible thresholds.
0.65, because it has the highest recall among the listed thresholds whose peak-day alert volume remains within capacity.

q: In a completed randomised experiment, a search assistant increases clicks per session while reducing successful application completion below the pre-agreed release floor. A teammate concludes that users must be clicking more because the interface has become confusing. The experiment establishes the metric changes, but the team has not inspected navigation paths or collected evidence about why additional clicks occur. Which statement is most defensible?
o: The extra clicks establish increased user engagement, so the variant should launch despite the task- completion requirement.
The results prove that interface confusion is the specific mechanism; redesign the interface without investigating alternative explanations.
The variant fails the completion guardrail, but the reason for the additional clicks remains unverified; investigate user journeys before selecting the remedy.
A randomised experiment cannot inform release decisions unless the team first proves the psychological reason for every changed metric.

q: A proposed architecture performs inference inside an entity's approved in-kingdom environment. However, its observability component exports raw prompts and retrieved case passages to a support platform abroad. The entity's handling rule requires all copies of Restricted content, including diagnostic logs, to remain in the approved environment. The support platform promises not to use customer data for training. What should the architecture reviewer require?
o: Bring diagnostic handling into compliance with the stated rule, such as keeping the Restricted logs inside the approved environment, before approving the complete data path.
Approve the design because the location of the model computation alone determines compliance for the entire application.
Approve the design because diagnostic copies are exempt from the handling rule when the vendor has a no-training commitment.
Sample only one in ten requests for export because reducing the number of logged records removes the location requirement.

q: A retrieval assistant is configured to prefer recent documents. An unverified document submitted through a general upload channel claims to be a new official circular and carries today's date. It ranks above an older authenticated circular, and the assistant presents its claims as current policy. The upload channel does not verify the issuing authority, but ingestion marks every uploaded document as authoritative. Which correction addresses the root cause?
o: Increase the recency weight so genuine new circulars will eventually outrank the unverified document.
Validate source authority and provenance before assigning policy-document status, and restrict authoritative retrieval to approved sources and valid versions.
Ask the model to judge whether a document's language sounds official and use that judgement as the authoritative status flag.
Raise the semantic-similarity threshold because an unverified document cannot be highly similar to a legitimate policy question.

q: An assistant passes its technical evaluation. Before launch, the operations team discovers that no team has accepted responsibility for reviewing escalated cases, correcting published guidance or authorising rollback during an incident. The proposal assumes that these decisions will be handled informally after launch. Existing manual service remains available. What is the most appropriate next step?
o: Launch because evaluation success establishes operational readiness, and assign responsibilities after the first incident reveals what is needed.
Make the model decide whether its own behaviour warrants rollback because it has access to the latest user conversations.
Transfer all responsibility to the vendor through a general support contract without confirming coverage for the entity's operational decisions.
Establish accountable owners, escalation procedures and decision authority as part of readiness approval before transferring the scope into live operation.

q: After a faulty release, a team restores the previous model weights but leaves the new feature transformer in place. Both transformers produce the same number of columns, but two feature meanings changed between versions. The model loads successfully, yet historical replay no longer matches the previously validated deployment. The registry stores the old weights but not their preprocessing version. What failed, and what should change?
o: The rollback did not restore the complete compatible inference bundle; version and deploy the model together with its preprocessing and required configuration.
The old weights have become incompatible with historical data because models naturally lose reproducibility as calendar time passes.
Successful loading proves compatibility, so the remaining prediction differences should be handled by adjusting the output threshold.
The old model should be retrained against the new transformer before attempting to reconstruct the previously validated release.

q: An assistant produces a syntactically valid JSON request to retrieve an application. The object passes the required schema, but its application identifier belongs to another user. The identifier appeared in an uploaded document. The backend currently executes every schema-valid request using a broad service account, without checking ownership against the authenticated session. Which change is necessary?
o: Strengthen the JSON schema's identifier format so every correctly shaped identifier can be assumed to belong to the current user.
Ask the assistant to state that it has verified ownership, then accept the tool request if that statement is present.
Validate the requested application's access rights against the authenticated user in backend code before executing the operation.
Remove the identifier from the assistant's final natural-language response while continuing to execute the original retrieval request.

q: A serving configuration has a combined input-and-output limit of 16,000 tokens. Its system instructions, conversation history and formatting overhead total 2,000 tokens. Retrieved passages add 12,000 tokens, and the application must reserve 3,000 tokens for the answer. These counts use the actual production tokenizer. Requests fail before generation, and the team proposes lowering temperature. Which correction follows from the evidence?
o: Lower temperature because deterministic generation reduces the number of tokens occupied by the input passages.
Keep the request unchanged because only retrieved text, rather than all input and reserved output, counts towards the stated limit.
Remove the system instructions and retain every retrieved passage because conversation controls are less important than document volume.
Reduce the retrieved-content budget to at most 11,000 tokens, preserve the required instructions and answer reserve, and validate the complete request budget.

q: A staff member's access to a sensitive programme is revoked. New retrieval requests correctly exclude its documents, but the assistant can still return programme details from a cached answer created while the staff member was authorised. The cache includes a user identifier but does not track permission changes or recheck access before reuse. What is the appropriate remediation?
o: Keep the cached response because a user who was previously authorised retains permanent permission to receive regenerated copies.
Make cache reuse respect current authorisation, invalidate affected entries on permission changes and prevent stale cached material from bypassing access checks.
Add more precise programme keywords to the search filter because the cached response must have come from a new retrieval failure.
Rotate the language model version because information stored in an application cache can be removed only by changing model weights.

q: An assistant operates reliably when exactly 20 conversations are active. During extended use, GPU memory rises even after users close conversations, while the number of active sessions stays near 20. A heap and allocator inspection shows that completed requests remain referenced in a session registry, retaining their KV-cache allocations. Restarting the service temporarily restores normal memory use. Which action addresses the recurring failure?
o: Correct session cleanup and release completed-request state, then verify that memory is reclaimed under repeated session turnover.
Reduce model temperature so completed requests become deterministic and their retained KV caches consume no additional memory.
Increase the active-session limit because the stable active count shows that the service has unused memory capacity.
Schedule regular restarts as the permanent fix while leaving completed sessions referenced indefinitely in the registry.

q: An eligibility model was trained under a policy that has now been formally replaced. Data-quality checks confirm that feature availability, units and serving transforms remain correct. An independent review applies the new policy to recent cases and finds systematic label changes for a defined applicant category even when its recorded characteristics are unchanged. The model continues reproducing the old policy's decisions. Which interpretation and response are most appropriate?
o: The source feed must be broken because unchanged model weights cannot produce a mismatch with newly reviewed outcomes.
The evaluation labels should be changed back to the old decisions so the monitored accuracy remains comparable over time.
The applicable feature-to-decision relationship has changed; version the policy and evaluation criteria, then update and validate the decision system against the new requirements.
The mismatch is exclusively a latency issue; move inference to a larger server before reviewing model or policy logic.

q: A new admission model appears to have similar recall across applicant groups. However, evaluation labels come only from applicants admitted by the previous system, because rejected applicants never received an independent qualification assessment. The new model will screen the full applicant population. The team wants to use the observed parity as proof that deployment will treat qualified applicants fairly across groups. What is the main limitation and appropriate next step?
o: Similar recall on previously admitted applicants proves parity for the full population because all groups appear in the evaluation set.
Assign every previously rejected applicant a negative qualification label so the evaluation can include the entire historical population.
Remove group identifiers from the audit dataset because measuring group differences introduces the disparity the team is trying to avoid.
The labelled sample is selected by earlier admission decisions; obtain trustworthy assessments from a representative sample covering previously admitted and rejected applicants before generalising.

q:
A transaction-review service must maximise recall while generating at most 200 alerts per day and maintaining precision of at least 45%. A representative daily evaluation contains 100 actual positive cases and yields the following results.
Threshold | Alerts | True positives | Precision | Recall
0.30 | 350 | 84 | 24% | 84%
0.45 | 200 | 80 | 40% | 80%
0.60 | 160 | 72 | 45% | 72%
0.75 | 100 | 60 | 60% | 60%
Which threshold should be selected?
o: 0.45, because using the full alert capacity takes precedence over the minimum precision requirement.
0.60, because it provides the highest recall among the thresholds satisfying both the alert- capacity limit and the precision floor.
0.75, because the highest precision automatically maximises recall once the capacity limit is met.
0.30, because the largest number of true positives is sufficient even when both operational conditions fail.

q: A retraining candidate passes schema and total-row-count checks. Its overall validation accuracy improves from 92% to 94%, but recall for an operationally critical supplier category falls from 81% to 63%. The approved release floor for that category is 75%. Investigation finds that duplicate records from large suppliers concealed a reduction in small-supplier coverage. The current promotion logic checks only total rows and aggregate accuracy. Which control change most directly prevents a repeat?
o: Raise the aggregate accuracy threshold to 94% and retain total row count as the sole data-coverage check.
Add training epochs whenever the critical category's recall falls, and allow promotion as long as the training job completes.
Add uniqueness and category-coverage checks before training and enforce the critical- category performance floor as a mandatory promotion gate.
Merge the critical category into the largest supplier group so the promotion dashboard reports a more stable recall estimate.

q:
A portal's observed peak is 140 requests per second. The selected model must achieve p90 latency no greater than 850 ms at that load and require a monthly provisioned-capacity cost no greater than SAR 45,000. All candidates meet hosting and explanation requirements. The approved objective is the highest F1 among feasible candidates. The chart shows the monthly cost of provisioning each candidate for the indicated sustained load.
Model | F1 | p90 at 140 requests per second
A | 0.83 | 740 ms
B | 0.88 | 790 ms
C | 0.90 | 830 ms
Which candidate should be selected?
o: Model B, because it meets both ceilings at the required peak and has the highest F1 among the feasible candidates.
Model C, because its cost is below the ceiling at 100 requests per second and it has the highest F1 overall.
Model A, because the objective requires the lowest cost even when a more accurate candidate also satisfies the constraints.
No candidate, because none simultaneously achieves the lowest cost and highest F1 of all three models.

q: A policy update has been ingested correctly. The old version is excluded from current-policy retrieval, and a fresh uncached request retrieves the replacement and generates the correct answer. Nevertheless, ordinary requests still receive the old rule. Inspection shows that the application serves cached answers before retrieval and that cache entries have no link to document or policy versions. Which change addresses the remaining failure?
o: Re-embed the replacement document repeatedly until its similarity score exceeds that of every historical version.
Lower the model's temperature because the correct uncached response indicates that generation variability is the main remaining problem.
Increase the number of retrieved passages even though cached requests return before the retrieval stage executes.
Invalidate answers affected by document changes and associate reusable answers with the relevant knowledge version or freshness policy.

q: A team fine-tunes an assistant using correctly serialised conversations. Training loss declines steadily, but held-out answer quality barely changes. Inspection of the training labels shows that loss is computed on user-message tokens while all assistant-answer tokens are masked out. The team proposes training for more epochs because the loss curve still improves. What should be corrected first?
o: Fix the loss mask so training optimises the intended assistant-answer tokens, then retrain and evaluate answer quality rather than relying on the existing loss trend.
Continue training until user-message prediction is nearly perfect because this necessarily establishes that assistant-answer behaviour has been learned.
Increase the inference temperature so the serving model can compensate for answer tokens excluded from the training objective.
Replace the evaluation questions with user-message completion tasks and treat the resulting score as evidence of improved answering.

q: An assistant's system prompt contains a live credential for an internal service. After a document-based injection causes disclosure during an authorised test, the team adds an output filter that blocks the complete credential string. A second test obtains fragments that can be combined to reconstruct it. The credential is needed by backend code, not by the model's language task. Which remediation addresses the underlying exposure?
o: Expand the output filter to cover more spellings and keep the same live credential in the prompt for backend convenience.
Place the credential earlier in the system prompt because higher-priority text cannot be reproduced in generated output.
Revoke or rotate the exposed credential, remove secrets from model-visible context and keep authentication in controlled backend code.
Encode the credential before inserting it into the prompt and treat the encoded form as safe to reveal to users.

q: An incident has been contained by restoring a validated deployment. Replay confirms that incompatible preprocessing caused incorrect scores for some applications with missing records. The team has not yet determined the complete affected population or downstream consequences. A status report is due to leadership, and a colleague proposes saying that every decision during the incident was wrong to emphasise urgency. What should the report state?
o: The system is fully resolved and no further review is needed because the previous deployment is serving traffic again.
Report the verified defect and containment, distinguish the known affected cases from the scope still under investigation, and identify owners for impact assessment and remediation.
State that every decision was wrong because a stronger claim is justified when it helps secure resources for corrective work.
Omit the incident until the complete impact is known because partial but qualified findings are unsuitable for leadership decisions.

q:
An entity must select one production model for a synchronous eligibility service. Before evaluation, stakeholders approved the following rule: maximise F1 among candidates with p90 latency at or below 1,000 ms at the observed peak of 180 requests per second, monthly cost at or below SAR 60,000, processing inside the approved environment and validated per-decision explanations. No requirement may be deferred until after launch. All measurements use the same evaluation set and intended workload.
Model | F1 | p90 at peak | Monthly cost | Approved environment | Explanation validation
A | 0.84 | 480 ms | SAR 28,000 | Yes | Passed
B | 0.88 | 890 ms | SAR 54,000 | Yes | Passed
C | 0.91 | 940 ms | SAR 59,000 | Yes | Not passed
D | 0.93 | 780 ms | SAR 57,000 | No | Passed
Which recommendation follows the approved rule?
o: Select Model D because its highest F1 and compliant latency and cost outweigh the unapproved processing environment.
Select Model C because explanation validation can be completed after launch without affecting the model's existing F1 score.
Select Model A because the cheapest and fastest feasible candidate must be preferred regardless of the approved quality objective.
Select Model B because it has the highest F1 among candidates satisfying every requirement; Model A is also feasible but has lower F1.

q: A fraud detection model must identify as many fraudulent transactions as possible. Missing fraud is much more costly than flagging a legitimate transaction. Which metric should be prioritized?
o: Accuracy
Precision
Recall
MSE
e: Clue: Missing fraud / identify as many as possible

q: A company wants an LLM to answer using internal policies that are updated every week without retraining the model frequently. What is MOST appropriate?
o: Fine-tuning
RAG
Increase temperature
Data augmentation
e: Clue: updated every week + without retraining

q: A model performs very well on training data but poorly on unseen data. What is the MOST likely issue?
o: Underfitting
Overfitting
Data encryption
High throughput
e: Clue: train good / unseen poor

q: After deployment, the distribution of incoming input data becomes different from the training data. What is this called?
o: Concept Drift
Data Drift
Data Leakage
Underfitting
e: Clue: input distribution changed

q: The relationship between customer behavior and the target outcome changes over time. What is this called?
o: Data Drift
Concept Drift
Data Leakage
Overfitting
e: Clue: relationship changed

q: A model accidentally used test-set information during training, producing unrealistically high evaluation scores. What is this?
o: Data Leakage
Data Drift
Concept Drift
Underfitting
e: Clue: test data used during training

q: A new model version is first deployed to 10% of users while 90% remain on the old version. Which strategy is used?
o: Blue-Green
Canary
Rollback
Vertical scaling
e: Clue: 10% of users first

q: Two identical production environments exist. The current version runs in one, the new version in the other, then traffic is fully switched. Which strategy?
o: Canary
Blue-Green
Rollback
A/B test
e: Clue: two environments + switched entirely

q: A release causes severe errors. The team immediately returns traffic to the last stable model version. What is this?
o: Rollback
Canary
Fine-tuning
Sharding
e: Clue: return to previous stable version

q: A hospital system must avoid missing patients who actually have a rare disease. Which metric is MOST important?
o: Precision
Recall
Latency
Accuracy
e: Clue: avoid missing patients

q: An AI system blocks accounts suspected of fraud. The company wants to minimize legitimate users being incorrectly blocked. Which metric?
o: Recall
Precision
RMSE
Throughput
e: Clue: legitimate users incorrectly blocked

q: An AI service can process many requests per second, but each individual request takes too long. What is the main problem?
o: Throughput
Latency
Recall
Accuracy
e: Clue: response time per request

q: To handle more inference traffic, a company adds more servers instead of upgrading a single server. What is this?
o: Vertical scaling
Horizontal scaling
Fine-tuning
Rollback
e: Clue: adds more servers

q: A company increases CPU and RAM on the same inference server. What type of scaling is this?
o: Horizontal
Vertical
Canary
Sharding
e: Clue: same server + more CPU/RAM

q: Only employees who need sensitive training data should receive access. Which principle is BEST?
o: Least Privilege
High Throughput
Data Augmentation
Fine-tuning
e: Clue: only employees who need access

q: Sensitive data is being sent from a client application to an AI server. Which protection is MOST appropriate?
o: Encryption in transit
Encryption at rest
Fine-tuning
Data augmentation
e: Clue: sent from client to server

q: Sensitive customer data is stored in a database. Which protection is MOST appropriate?
o: Encryption at rest
Encryption in transit
Canary deployment
Model retraining
e: Clue: stored in database

q: A system needs to record who accessed the AI platform, what they changed, and when. Which feature?
o: Audit Logs
Fine-tuning
Caching
Quantization
e: Clue: who + what + when

q: A company wants to verify a user identity before login. What is this?
o: Authorization
Authentication
Encryption
Auditing
e: Clue: verify identity

q: A logged-in user requests access to the admin dashboard. The system checks whether that user has permission. What is this?
o: Authentication
Authorization
Encryption
Auditing
e: Clue: permission / allowed to access

q: A team needs to track model versions and mark which version is approved for production. What tool is MOST appropriate?
o: Model Registry
Feature Store
Vector Database
Cache
e: Clue: model versions + approved for production

q: A team wants reusable, consistent features for both model training and online inference. Which component helps MOST?
o: Model Registry
Feature Store
CDN
Audit Log
e: Clue: reusable features training + inference

q: An LLM produces inconsistent creative answers. The company wants more deterministic outputs. What should it do?
o: Increase temperature
Decrease temperature
Increase data drift
Disable monitoring
e: Clue: more deterministic / less random

q: A policy assistant often invents facts. The company has a trusted internal knowledge base. Which approach BEST reduces hallucinations?
o: Increase temperature
RAG with trusted sources
Disable citations
Remove retrieval
e: Clue: hallucinations + trusted knowledge

q: A company wants its model to consistently answer in a specialized legal tone and format, using many labeled examples. Which approach is MOST suitable?
o: RAG only
Fine-tuning
Horizontal scaling
Encryption
e: Clue: change tone/format behavior

q: A classification dataset has 99% negative examples and 1% positive examples. Which statement is MOST accurate?
o: Accuracy alone can be misleading
Accuracy is always sufficient
Recall is irrelevant
Class imbalance improves fairness
e: Clue: 99% vs 1% class imbalance

q: A model performs poorly on both training and test data. What is MOST likely?
o: Overfitting
Underfitting
Data Drift
High Precision
e: Clue: poor on both train and test

q: A regression team wants a metric that penalizes large errors more heavily. Which metric?
o: MAE
MSE
Recall
Precision
e: Clue: penalizes large errors

q: A regression team wants an error metric in the same unit as the target while still penalizing large errors. Which?
o: RMSE
MSE
F1
Accuracy
e: Clue: same unit + penalize large errors

q: A model needs a robust estimate of performance on a relatively small dataset. Which technique is MOST useful?
o: Cross-validation
Single train split only
Disable validation
Increase temperature
e: Clue: small dataset + robust estimate

q: A team adjusts hyperparameters using the test set repeatedly. What is the main risk?
o: Test leakage / biased final evaluation
Higher throughput
Better security
Lower latency
e: Clue: hyperparameters + test set repeatedly

q: A team wants to reduce overfitting by penalizing large weights. Which technique?
o: Regularization
Data leakage
Rollback
Sharding
e: Clue: reduce overfitting + penalize weights

q: Which technique may force some model weights exactly to zero and encourage sparsity?
o: L1 regularization
L2 regularization
Batch inference
Caching
e: Clue: weights to zero / sparsity

q: A transformer needs to determine which tokens in a sequence are most relevant to each other. Which mechanism?
o: Attention
Sharding
Encryption
Rollback

The Ministry of Social Development is deploying a model to pre-screen citizen applications for a housing support programme. The model produces a risk score; applications flagged as high-risk are routed to a manual verification team, and the remainder proceed to automated approval.

- The verification team can process 400 applications per day; average daily volume is 9,000 applications.
- The end-to-end API response must stay under 800 ms at p95, because the model is called synchronously inside the existing application portal.
- Annual inference budget is capped at SAR 350,000.
- Any decision that results in rejection or additional verification of a citizen must be explainable to the affected individual on request.
Three candidates were evaluated on the same held-out set of 120,000 historical applications:
Metric | Model A | Model B | Model C
Architecture | Logistic regression | Gradient boosting | Fine-tuned LLM
ROC-AUC | 0.81 | 0.89 | 0.91
Recall @ 400 flags/day | 0.44 | 0.63 | 0.66
p95 latency | 40 ms | 120 ms | 2,400 ms
Annual inference cost | SAR 20,000 | SAR 60,000 | SAR 1,900,000
Per-decision explanation | Native coefficients | SHAP values | Free-text, not verifiable
Which model should be recommended for production, and on what basis?
o: Model C, because it has the highest AUC and recall, and the budget can be revisited in the next fiscal cycle.
Model B, because it satisfies the latency and budget constraints, provides verifiable per-decision explanations, and delivers the highest recall among the compliant options.
Model A, because it is the cheapest and fastest, and its explanations are the most direct.
Model C for scoring with Model A running in parallel to generate the explanations shown to citizens.
e: Requirements matching: Model C fails latency (2,400 ms), budget and explainability. Among models meeting every hard constraint (A and B), pick the one with the highest recall: Model B.

You operate a document-classification service on a single GPU. It is called synchronously by a case-management system with an agreed SLO: p95 latency below 1,500 ms. Peak load is 60 requests per second.
To improve GPU utilisation, your team ran a load test sweeping the maximum batch size:
Batch size | Throughput (req/s) | p95 latency (ms) | GPU utilisation
1 | 2.1 | 480 | 21%
2 | 3.8 | 610 | 34%
4 | 5.2 | 890 | 52%
8 | 6.6 | 1,420 | 71%
16 | 7.4 | 2,050 | 88%
32 | 7.8 | 2,600 | 94%
Given the SLO and the peak load, what is the correct configuration decision?
o: Use batch size 32 to maximise GPU utilisation, and negotiate a relaxed SLO with the case-management team.
Use batch size 8 as the operating point, and provision replicas based on 6.6 req/s each to cover the 60 req/s peak with headroom.
Use batch size 1 to minimise latency, since latency is the binding constraint in a synchronous integration.
Use batch size 16, since 2,050 ms is close enough to the SLO and it delivers higher throughput per GPU.
e: Largest batch that still meets the SLO is 8 (1,420 ms < 1,500 ms). Replicas needed = 60 / 6.6 = 9.1, so provision at least 10 for headroom.
